title: India to have adequate coking coal as Europe, US move away from blast furnaces: Naveen Jindal
dek: Naveen Jindal says India will have adequate coking coal as Europe and the US move away from blast furnaces, but urges continued investment in overseas coal assets.
summary: According to Mint, Naveen Jindal, chairman of Jindal Steel Ltd, said India will have adequate coking coal as Europe and the US shift away from blast furnaces. He advised that the industry must keep investing in overseas coal assets to secure supplies.
keyFacts: Naveen Jindal is chairman of Jindal Steel Ltd
He advised continued investment in overseas coal assets to secure supplies
whyItMatters: India's blast-furnace-led expansion relies heavily on imported coking coal, and reduced Western demand could ease competition for supply.
implications: Indian producers may weigh equity stakes in overseas mines, and coal traders should watch how shifting Western demand affects seaborne coking coal flows.
publisherExcerpt: The industry must continue investing in overseas coal assets to secure supplies, advises Naveen Jindal, chairman, Jindal Steel Ltd
